questions.question: Name four animals people used for transport, and explain what a pack animal is.
questions.expected_answer: Oxen, horses, donkeys and mules. A pack animal is an animal that carries loads tied onto its back.

questions.question: Describe an ox-wagon and name three groups of people who used one.
questions.expected_answer: An ox-wagon had four big wooden wheels with iron rims and often a canvas cover. It was pulled slowly by a span of twelve to sixteen oxen. It was used by farmers, traders, hunters, missionaries, Voortrekkers and transport riders carrying goods to the mines.

questions.question: What is the difference between a cart and a coach? Give one problem of animal transport.
questions.expected_answer: A cart is a small vehicle, usually with two wheels, pulled by one or two animals and used for goods or a few people. A coach is a large closed vehicle pulled by a team of horses or mules that carried passengers and post. Animals needed food, water and rest, travel was slow, and animals could die of diseases such as rinderpest.
